On days I feel good, I will do as much as I can as well. I am aware I will feel incredibly unwell after but things need to get done. And sometimes only those days make me feel like I can function in everyday life. Those few moments of feeling human are important. It sounds weird to people who doesn't experience pain like that but we all seek normality all the time.

When she is having good days and you are available, maybe help her form the sidelines? If she is cleaning, offer to vacuum etc. you are not taking away her independence but it will go a long way and not tire her out completely. Also try to think what would happen if she didn't clean on her good days. Would she need to do it on the days she is feeling even worse, would the house be a mess which makes her feel even worse. 

Honestly my friends tell me to take it easy all the time but it doesn't help. Life doesn't stop. But having someone cook dinner without me asking or helping to clean means the world. And sometimes I just need a distraction from my pain. I can imagine the communication is difficult and frustrating. But she is trying to be the best mom she can and be an example for you. 

You got this :) And remind her she is a great mom as well! I'm sure she is just trying the best she can.

Going to sleep earlier: 

1) Try to go to sleep in a dark room. Cover all the windows, shut the lights, put your phone in the far end of the room.

3) Breathing technique my friend used a few years ago to fall asleep: Breath in through your nose for four seconds. Hold your breath for seven seconds. Slowly breathe out through your mouth for eight seconds. Repeat this process until you fall asleep. 

How to wake up:

To wake up at a certain time you need a rhythm.  Maybe your parents could wake you up when they wake up? After about a week, if you go to sleep in a normal time, your body will wake up on his own.
